source_text: Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος τῷ Χαρίτωνι εἶπεν· Ἔτι εἰπὲ, Χαρίτων, καὶ σὺ Χριστιανὸς εἶ; Χαρίτων εἶπε· Χριστιανός εἰμι Θεοῦ κελεύσει. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος πρὸς τὴν Χαριτὼ εἶπε· Σὺ τί λέγεις, Χαριτώ; Χαριτὼ εἶπε· Χριστιανός εἰμι τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ δωρεᾷ. Ῥουστικὸς εἶπε τῷ Εὐελπίστῳ· Σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ; Εὐέλπιστος, δοῦλος Καίσαρος, ἀπεκρίνατο· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι ἐλευθερωθεὶς ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς ἐλπίδος μετέχω χάριτι Χριστοῦ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος τῷ Ἱέρακι εἶπε· Καὶ σὺ Χριστιανὸς εἶ; Ἱέραξ εἶπεν· Ναὶ, Χριστιανός εἰμι, τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν Θεὸν σέβομαι καὶ προσκυνῶ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ἰουστῖνος ὑμᾶς ἐποίησε Χριστιανούς; Ἱέραξ εἶπεν· Ἤμην Χριστιανὸς, καὶ ἔσομαι. Παίων δὲ ἑστὼς εἶπε· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Τίς ὁ διδάξας σε; Παίων εἶπεν· Ἀπὸ τῶν γονέων παρειλήφαμεν τὴν καλὴν ταύτην ὁμολογίαν. Εὐέλπιστος εἶπεν· Ἰουστίνου μὲν ἡδέως ἤκουον τῶν λόγων. Παρὰ τῶν γονέων δὲ κἀγὼ παρείληφα Χριστιανὸς εἶναι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Ποῦ εἰσιν οἱ γονεῖς σου; Εὐέλπιστος εἶπεν· Ἐν τῇ Καππαδοκίᾳ. Ῥουστικὸς τῷ Ἱέρακι λέγει· Οἱ σοὶ γονεῖς ποῦ εἰσίν; ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο λέγων· Ὁ ἀληθινὸς ἡμῶν πατήρ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ μήτηρ ἡ εἰς αὐτὸν πίστις· οἱ δὲ ἐπίγειοί μου γονεῖς ἐτελεύτησαν. Καὶ ἐγὼ, ἀπὸ Ἰκονίου τῆς Φρυγίας ἀποσπασθεὶς, ἐνθάδε ἐλήλυθα. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε Λιβεριανῷ· Τί καὶ σὺ λέγεις, Χριστιανὸς εἶ; οὐδὲ σὺ εὐσεβεῖς; Λιβεριανὸς εἶπε· Κἀγὼ Χριστιανός εἰμι· εὐσεβῶ γὰρ καὶ προσκυνῶ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεόν.
thought_title: Each companion confesses Christ before the prefect
orientation: The prefect Rusticus turns from Justin to each of his companions in turn, asking whether they too are Christians and where their parents are.
pass_a_gloss: Rusticus [the] prefect said to Chariton: Still say, Chariton, also you a Christian are? Chariton said: A Christian I am by God's command. Rusticus [the] prefect to Charito said: You what say, Charito? Charito said: A Christian I am by the gift of God. Rusticus said to Euelpistus: You then who are? Euelpistus, a slave of Caesar, answered: I too a Christian am, having been set free by Christ, and of the same hope I share by the grace of Christ. Rusticus [the] prefect to Hierax said: Also you a Christian are? Hierax said: Yes, a Christian I am, for the same God I worship and adore. Rusticus [the] prefect said: Justin made you Christians? Hierax said: I was a Christian, and I will be. Paeon then standing said: I too a Christian am. Rusticus [the] prefect said: Who [is] the one who taught you? Paeon said: From [our] parents we received this good confession. Euelpistus said: Of Justin indeed gladly I listened to [his] words. From [my] parents then I too received to be a Christian. Rusticus [the] prefect said: Where are your parents? Euelpistus said: In Cappadocia. Rusticus to Hierax says: Your parents where are? He then answered saying: The true father of us is Christ, and mother the faith in him; but my earthly parents have died. And I, from Iconium of Phrygia having been torn away, here have come. Rusticus [the] prefect said to Liberianus: What also you say? A Christian are you? Not even you worship? Liberianus said: I too a Christian am; for I worship and adore the only true God.

choices.why: Dative of means; keeps the sense that Chariton's Christian identity is not his own doing but God's ordering.
Dative of means; Charito attributes her Christian state to divine gift, matching the glossary sense of χάρισμα as divine gift.

choices.english: having been set free by Christ
choices.why: Passive participle with agent; Euelpistus, though Caesar's slave, claims a higher freedom from Christ.

choices.term: τῆς αὐτῆς ἐλπίδος μετέχω χάριτι Χριστοῦ
choices.english: of the same hope I share by the grace of Christ
choices.why: Keeps the genitive of the thing shared and the dative of means; the hope is the common Christian hope.
rejected: I partake of the same hope through Christ's grace
I share in the same hope by Christ's favor

choices.term: τὸν γὰρ αὐτὸν Θεὸν σέβομαι καὶ προσκυνῶ
choices.english: for the same God I worship and adore
choices.why: Two verbs distinguished: σέβομαι as reverent worship, προσκυνέω as adoration; Hierax claims continuity with Justin's God.
rejected: for I revere and bow down to the same God
for I worship and venerate the same God

choices.why: Glossary term ὁμολογία rendered as confession; καλὴν as good, not beautiful, to convey moral worth.

pass_b_english: The prefect Rusticus said to Chariton, "Tell me further, Chariton: are you also a Christian?" Chariton said, "I am a Christian by God's command." The prefect Rusticus said to Charito, "What do you say, Charito?" Charito said, "I am a Christian by the gift of God." Rusticus said to Euelpistus, "And who are you?" Euelpistus, a slave of Caesar, answered, "I too am a Christian, having been set free by Christ, and I share in the same hope by the grace of Christ." The prefect Rusticus said to Hierax, "Are you also a Christian?" Hierax said, "Yes, I am a Christian, for I worship and adore the same God." The prefect Rusticus said, "Did Justin make you Christians?" Hierax said, "I was a Christian, and I will remain one." Paeon, standing by, said, "I too am a Christian." The prefect Rusticus said to Paeon, "Who taught you?" Paeon said, "We received this good confession from our parents." Euelpistus said, "I listened gladly to Justin's words, but I too received being a Christian from my parents." The prefect Rusticus said, "Where are your parents?" Euelpistus said, "In Cappadocia." Rusticus said to Hierax, "Where are your parents?" He answered, "Our true father is Christ, and our mother is faith in him. My earthly parents have died. As for me, I was torn away from Iconium in Phrygia and came here." The prefect Rusticus said to Liberianus, "What do you say? Are you a Christian? Do you not worship?" Liberianus said, "I too am a Christian, for I worship and adore the only true God."

last_rejected.why: 'Torn away' captures ἀποσπασθείς well. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀποσπασθείς means 'torn away/separated'; translation is accurate within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: We received this good confession from our parents
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἀπὸ τῶν γονέων παρειλήφαμεν τὴν καλὴν ταύτην ὁμολογίαν
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'confession' for ὁμολογία. English uses 'confession' — correct! No violation.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁμολογία means 'confession'; English 'confession' matches source and glossary correctly.

last_rejected.quote: I too received being a Christian from my parents
last_rejected.source_quote: Παρὰ τῶν γονέων δὲ κἀγὼ παρείληφα Χριστιανὸς εἶναι
last_rejected.why: English 'received being a Christian' is awkward but conveys 'received to be a Christian'. No meaning error.
last_rejected.ruling: παρείληφα Χριστιανὸς εἶναι = 'received to be a Christian'; awkward but meaning preserved.

problems.quote: The prefect Rusticus said, "Who taught you?"
problems.why: Rusticus's question 'Who taught you?' is directed at Paeon, but the preceding speech is Paeon's; the 'you' could be singular or plural, unclear.
problems.fix: Clarify that Rusticus turns to Paeon specifically.

edits.old: The prefect Rusticus said, "Who taught you?"
edits.new: The prefect Rusticus said to Paeon, "Who taught you?"

fixed: Added 'to Paeon' to clarify that Rusticus's question is directed at Paeon, matching the source's singular address.

problems.why: Same person appears as 'Chariton' then 'Charito' in adjacent lines; reader may think two women.
problems.fix: Standardize to one form, note variant.

problems.why: Unclear if Paeon is one of the six martyrs or a bystander; not addressed by Rusticus directly.
problems.fix: Clarify Paeon is a seventh companion or bystander.

problems.quote: I was a Christian, and I will be
problems.why: Hierax's tense sequence is paradoxical; probably means 'I was and I will remain.'
problems.fix: 'I was a Christian, and I will remain one'.

problems.quote: We received this good confession from our parents
problems.why: Paeon answers alone but says 'we'; unclear if he means himself and siblings or all Christians.
problems.fix: Clarify whether 'we' means Paeon and Euelpistus or a broader 'we'.

variants.text: We received this good confession from our parents

edits.old: I was a Christian, and I will be.
edits.new: I was a Christian, and I will remain one.

fixed: Chariton/Charito: The source uses two distinct names, Χαρίτων (Chariton, masculine) and Χαριτώ (Charito, feminine), for two different people. The English correctly renders them as 'Chariton' and 'Charito'. No edit needed.

Paeon: The source says Παίων δὲ ἑστὼς εἶπε, 'Paeon, standing by, said'. The English 'Paeon, standing by, said' accurately renders this. The source does not clarify whether he is a companion or bystander, so no edit is needed.

Hierax's tense: The source says Ἤμην Χριστιανὸς, καὶ ἔσομαι, 'I was a Christian, and I will be'. The English 'I was a Christian, and I will be' is a literal rendering. The suggested 'I will remain one' clarifies the meaning without changing the source. Edit made.

Paeon's 'we': The source says Ἀπὸ τῶν γονέων παρειλήφαμεν τὴν καλὴν ταύτην ὁμολογίαν, 'From our parents we received this good confession'. The English 'We received this good confession from our parents' accurately renders the plural 'we'. The source does not specify who 'we' refers to, so no edit is needed.
